title.en: Do differences divide or enrich politics?

text.en: In your class, children differ in gender, religion and caste. How should politics deal with these differences? This chapter looks at how they shape and are shaped by politics.

Sexual division of labour means household work is done mostly by women while men do paid work outside, though both can do either. This is a social role, not natural.
Women's movements demanded equal rights, the vote and equal pay. Women's representation in legislatures is still low in India.
The Equal Remuneration Act 1976 says equal wages for equal work for men and women.
Reservation of one-third of seats for women in local bodies has increased their presence. A demand continues for similar reservation in legislatures.
Communalism means treating religion as the basis of the community and politics. It is a problem when religion is mixed with state power.
India is a secular state, which means no official religion and equal freedom for all faiths.
Caste has played a role in politics through caste groups, alliances and voting. But caste cannot decide every election, as people vote on other issues too.
Caste inequalities are slowly changing through education, urbanisation and law, but discrimination still exists.

problem.en: A legislature has 150 seats. If one-third were reserved for women, how many seats?

why.en: Today the share is lower in many legislatures.

prompt.en: Explain why communalism is dangerous in politics.

commonMisconceptions.en: Thinking religion has no place in life

points.en: Caste influences but does not decide politics.
